ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the rhombus $ABCD$ has a side length of $10$, and $\angle A=60^\circ$. By successively connecting the midpoints of each side of the rhombus $ABCD$, quadrilateral ${A}_{1}{B}_{1}{C}_{1}{D}_{1}$ is obtained; by successively connecting the midpoints of each side of quadrilateral ${A}_{1}{B}_{1}{C}_{1}{D}_{1}$, quadrilateral ${A}_{2}{B}_{2}{C}_{2}{D}_{2}$ is obtained; by successively connecting the midpoints of each side of quadrilateral ${A}_{2}{B}_{2}{C}_{2}{D}_{2}$, quadrilateral ${A}_{3}{B}_{3}{C}_{3}{D}_{3}$ is obtained; and so on. Following this pattern, what is the perimeter of the quadrilateral ${A}_{2n}{B}_{2n}{C}_{2n}{D}_{2n}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} By utilizing the properties of mid-quadrilaterals, we know quadrilaterals $A_{1}B_{1}C_{1}D_{1}$ and $A_{3}B_{3}C_{3}D_{3}$ are rectangles, while $A_{2}B_{2}C_{2}D_{2}$ and $A_{4}B_{4}C_{4}D_{4}$ are rhombuses.\\
Since the side length of rhombus ABCD is 10, and $\angle A=60^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\triangle ADB$ and $\triangle AA_{1}D_{1}$ are equilateral triangles, and the perimeter of rhombus ABCD is $10\times 4=40$;\\
therefore, the perimeter of rhombus $A_{2}B_{2}C_{2}D_{2}$ is $\frac{1}{2}\times 40=20$;\\
The perimeter of rhombus $A_{4}B_{4}C_{4}D_{4}$ is $\frac{1}{{2}^{2}}\times 40$;\\
$ \dots $\\
therefore, the perimeter of quadrilateral ${A}_{2n}{B}_{2n}{C}_{2n}{D}_{2n}$ is $40\times \frac{1}{{2}^{n}}=5\times 8\times \frac{1}{{2}^{n}}=\boxed{\frac{5}{{2}^{n-3}}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the rhombus $ABCD$ has a side length of $10$, and $\angle A=60^\circ$. By successively connecting the midpoints of each side of the rhombus $ABCD$, quadrilateral ${A}_{1}{B}_{1}{C}_{1}{D}_{1}$ is obtained; by successively connecting the midpoints of each side of quadrilateral ${A}_{1}{B}_{1}{C}_{1}{D}_{1}$, quadrilateral ${A}_{2}{B}_{2}{C}_{2}{D}_{2}$ is obtained; by successively connecting the midpoints of each side of quadrilateral ${A}_{2}{B}_{2}{C}_{2}{D}_{2}$, quadrilateral ${A}_{3}{B}_{3}{C}_{3}{D}_{3}$ is obtained; and so on. Following this pattern, what is the perimeter of the quadrilateral ${A}_{2n}{B}_{2n}{C}_{2n}{D}_{2n}$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} By utilizing the properties of mid-quadrilaterals, we know quadrilaterals $A_{1}B_{1}C_{1}D_{1}$ and $A_{3}B_{3}C_{3}D_{3}$ are rectangles, while $A_{2}B_{2}C_{2}D_{2}$ and $A_{4}B_{4}C_{4}D_{4}$ are rhombuses.\\
Since the side length of rhombus ABCD is 10, and $\angle A=60^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\triangle ADB$ and $\triangle AA_{1}D_{1}$ are equilateral triangles, and the perimeter of rhombus ABCD is $10\times 4=40$;\\
therefore, the perimeter of rhombus $A_{2}B_{2}C_{2}D_{2}$ is $\frac{1}{2}\times 40=20$;\\
The perimeter of rhombus $A_{4}B_{4}C_{4}D_{4}$ is $\frac{1}{{2}^{2}}\times 40$;\\
$ \dots $\\
therefore, the perimeter of quadrilateral ${A}_{2n}{B}_{2n}{C}_{2n}{D}_{2n}$ is $40\times \frac{1}{{2}^{n}}=5\times 8\times \frac{1}{{2}^{n}}=\boxed{\frac{5}{{2}^{n-3}}}$.
raw_record.final_cot: The figure is an outer rhombus ABCD, with A on the left, B at the bottom, C on the right, and D at the top; after connecting the midpoints of each side in order, A1B1C1D1 is obtained, then continuing to connect midpoints obtains A2B2C2D2, A3B3C3D3, and the figures alternate between “rectangle—rhombus.” Given AB=AD=10 and ∠A=60°, △ABD is an equilateral triangle with side length 10, so BD=10; also, from the properties of a rhombus, the other diagonal AC=10√3 can be obtained. According to the midpoint quadrilateral theorem, A1B1C1D1 is a rectangle, and its two sides are respectively half of the two diagonals of the original rhombus, namely 5 and 5√3, so its diagonal length is 10. Then take the midpoint quadrilateral A2B2C2D2 of A1B1C1D1, which is a rhombus, and its side length equals half of the diagonal of this rectangle, so the side length is 5 and the perimeter is 20. Every two “taking midpoints” operations, the perimeter becomes half of the original, therefore the perimeter of A2nB2nC2nD2n is 40/2^n, and can also be written as 5/2^(n-3).
